inspection_summary: Inspected all 936 logical lines. Lines 1–462 give a usable English article developing rational linear forms in odd zeta values, their improved arithmetic denominators, contour/saddle asymptotics, coefficient bounds, and parameter choices for irrationality and linear-independence results. Lines 464–935 are a complete Russian-language duplicate of that article, with lossy transliteration and the same formula-extraction damage, so they add no distinct semantic mechanism; both bibliographies and all front matter were also checked. Nine conservative units retain the recoverable conceptual chain while flagging every formula-dependent span for scan/PDF verification.

accepted_units.title: From isolated irrationality results to dimension growth for odd zeta values
accepted_units.why_material: The introduction reframes the target from proving individual irrationalities to producing lower bounds for the dimension of the span of 1 and odd zeta values, making explicit the collective linear-independence objective that governs the construction.
accepted_units.context_note: Retains the prior-results comparison and the definition of the dimension quantity needed to understand why later linear forms are evaluated collectively rather than one value at a time.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Mostly recoverable prose; exact displayed ranges and the notation for the dimension function should be checked against the typeset source before quotation.

accepted_units.title: Finite irrationality panels and the four-stage proof architecture
accepted_units.why_material: The stated theorems turn a single family of linear forms into finite-panel irrationality and dimension conclusions, while the roadmap isolates the reusable stages: saddle analysis, arithmetic denominator improvement, coefficient asymptotics, and a linear-independence criterion.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the theorem statements and the author’s own dependency map; the later units supply each advertised stage.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The prose architecture is reliable, but formula-extracted index ranges, inequalities, and constants in the theorem statements require PDF verification.

accepted_units.title: Symmetric rational functions produce linear forms supported only on odd zeta values
accepted_units.why_material: A parameterized rational function is differentiated and summed at integers; partial fractions plus its reflection parity cancel unwanted terms and express the result as a rational linear form in a controlled band of odd zeta values. This is the central representation change from a hypergeometric-type sum to arithmetic information.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the parameter inequalities, reflection identity, partial-fraction consequence, and initial denominator scale because removing any one would obscure why the support and arithmetic control have their stated form.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High formula dependence: product limits, exponents, derivative orders, signs, and coefficient indices contain extraction artifacts. The mechanism is recoverable from prose, but exact formulas must be verified from the PDF.

accepted_units.title: Prime-adic factorial minima save an exponential denominator factor
accepted_units.why_material: Lemma 1 refines the naive least-common-multiple denominator by extracting a product over primes whose valuations are minima of factorial-ratio valuations; a periodic floor-function analysis and the prime number theorem then give its exponential rate. This arithmetic saving is one of the independent budgets later balanced against analytic decay.
accepted_units.context_note: The full proof span is retained because the decomposition into derivative factors, integrality of normalized partial-fraction coefficients, prime-wise minimization, and asymptotic evaluation jointly justify the saving.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Very high formula risk: superscripts, radicals, floor-function interval endpoints, product ranges, and several symbols are garbled or displaced. Use this unit for the conceptual p-adic mechanism only until every exact identity is checked against the scan/PDF.

accepted_units.title: Cotangent residues convert the differentiated sum into a vertical contour integral
accepted_units.why_material: A higher cotangent derivative supplies the required pole principal parts, so residue calculus represents the discrete derivative sum by a vertical contour integral; decay of the rational function removes the other sides of an expanding rectangle. This creates the analytic form needed for saddle analysis.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes both the residue identity and the contour-vanishing argument, since the integral representation is not justified by the local pole expansion alone.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The strategic residue argument is readable, but derivative normalization, contour endpoints, half-integer coordinates, orientations, and signs are formula-sensitive and include extraction corruption; verify them in the typeset source.

accepted_units.title: Stirling scaling separates phase and amplitude and decomposes the integral by frequencies
accepted_units.why_material: After scaling by n and applying Stirling’s formula, the contour integral is expressed through an exponential phase and amplitude. A polynomial identity for the trigonometric factor decomposes it into frequency-indexed integrals whose saddle equation becomes an algebraic root problem.
accepted_units.context_note: Keeps the branch-cut convention, phase/amplitude definitions, trigonometric decomposition, and saddle equation together because they determine which stationary points are admissible and how their contributions compare.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High formula and branch-choice dependence: powers, square-root factors, summation restrictions, conjugations, and logarithm branches are vulnerable to extraction errors. The representation change is usable, but exact asymptotics require PDF verification.

accepted_units.title: Saddle geometry selects the unique dominant exponential rate of the linear forms
accepted_units.why_material: Under an explicit root-separation condition, the paper classifies all relevant real and complex saddle solutions on a closed level curve, deforms contours through them, applies Laplace asymptotics, and shows that only the outer admissible frequencies determine the exponential rate of the linear form.
accepted_units.context_note: Combines Lemmas 4–6 because the final rate depends on the preceding uniqueness, geometry, and contour-selection claims rather than on a formal stationary-phase substitution alone.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Substantial diagram/contour and formula dependence: the deformation description contains broken radicals and isolated artifacts, and the root condition and rate formula have damaged exponents. Verify exact paths, hypotheses, and constants from the PDF; the qualitative selection mechanism is recoverable.

accepted_units.title: A second saddle regime sharpens coefficient growth estimates
accepted_units.why_material: Crude derivative bounds first control all rational coefficients, then auxiliary horizontal contour integrals and a saddle associated with a minimal imaginary root sharpen their exponential growth rate. This supplies the coefficient-size budget required by the later independence criterion and distinguishes it from the saddle controlling linear-form smallness.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes Lemmas 7 and 8 and their bridge through auxiliary integrals so the sharpened bound is not detached from how coefficients enter those integrals.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High formula dependence: derivative powers, factorial ratios, integral powers, root notation, and exponential-rate exponents are corrupted in places. Treat numerical or symbolic transcription as provisional pending PDF verification.

accepted_units.title: Balancing denominator saving, analytic decay, and coefficient growth yields irrationality conclusions
accepted_units.why_material: The conclusion combines the arithmetic saving and saddle rate in a strict negativity condition, then chooses parameter families to force finite-panel irrationality and applies a linear-independence criterion to convert the rate comparison into dimension bounds. It shows how the abstract budgets drive concrete theorem design.
accepted_units.context_note: Retains the explicit parameter-selection discussion because it is the evidence that the preceding construction is tunable rather than merely asymptotic formalism.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The governing balance is readable, but extracted constants, parameter powers, logarithm bases, numerical approximations, and displayed bounds must be checked against the typeset source before reuse.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: The three-budget irrationality engine
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: The proof strategy is a tunable balance among prime-adic denominator saving, exponential smallness of the linear form, and exponential growth of its coefficients; irrationality or dimension gain appears only when the combined rate crosses the criterion’s strict threshold.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: This is a structural synthesis of the paper’s dependency chain, not an independently verified general criterion; exact rates and signs remain scan/PDF dependent.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Symmetry as a parity filter before asymptotics
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Reflection parity in the rational function and the matching cotangent residue kernel constrain the linear form to odd zeta values before saddle analysis, so analytic estimation operates on an arithmetically pre-filtered support.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The exact cancellation and residue normalizations cannot be certified from the damaged formulas alone.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Different saddle geometries govern usefulness and cost
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: The saddle selected for decay of the linear form and the imaginary-root saddle used to bound coefficient growth encode distinct sides of the same construction, making their rate comparison more informative than either asymptotic in isolation.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The relationship is supported within this source’s construction; it should not be generalized to other irrationality methods without separate evidence.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Parameter design maps a collective linear form to finite irrationality panels
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: The theorem families arise by choosing parameters so the odd-zeta support lands on a desired interval while the combined exponential budget stays favorable, converting a collective linear form into at-least-one-irrational conclusions rather than identifying a particular irrational value.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: Exact panel endpoints and numerical parameter checks require verification from the typeset article.

stop_reason: All 936 logical lines were inspected. The English mathematical text is represented from framing through construction, denominator arithmetic, contour conversion, both saddle analyses, coefficient bounds, and final parameter balancing. The remaining mathematical half is a claim-for-claim Russian translation with worse transliteration/formula extraction, while lines 431–472 and 907–936 are references or front matter; further units would therefore duplicate represented mechanisms or rely on defective formulas.
